zh.title: 借过一本有争议的书，应该怎样交代？
zh.deck: 说清借了什么，并不会取消原创。把借来的东西说成独立发现，才会让读者失去判断的地方。

sections.heading: 写作时，手边还有一本书
paragraphs: 接着写《红楼梦》的时候，我手边不只有前八十回和脂批。还有一种常被叫作“癸酉本”的文字，接在八十回之后，写了二十八回。它的来历有很大争议。我读过它，也借过它，这件事应该在读者面前说清。
困难不只是要不要提书名。写完以后，人很容易只记得自己最后怎样改，把最初在哪里受到提示忘在身后。一个场面换了人物，一段情节变了方向，写得越久，就越像从头到尾都是自己想出来的。
所以需要回过头去看：最早那一笔，究竟是从哪里来的？“后来已经写得很不一样”，可以说明改写的程度，不能代替对来路的回答。

sections.heading: 先不让身世替文字增添分量
paragraphs: 癸酉本自2008年起在网上流传，后来有过不同的排印与整理文本。关于它出自何时、出自谁手，公开说法并不一致，声称依据的旧稿也没有公开供人核验。公开研究多把它看作今人伪托。这些不是可以为了方便取材而跳过的小事。
本项目把它理解为后人依据某一版旧稿的再创作。这里要特别说清：这是我采用的工作假说，不是已经考定的身世；读者不接受它，也不妨碍检查我究竟借了什么。
我不在这组散文里为它辨真伪，并不意味着真伪无关紧要。若一份文字只是现代续写，它就不能凭自称古本，为曹雪芹原来的安排作证。文学上觉得合适，与历史上能够证明，是两种资格。
把这两种资格分开以后，反而能比较踏实地读它：一个场面可以启发写作，却不因此变成失稿的证据；一个细节与前八十回相合，也可能是后来的作者读得仔细，不能仅凭相合，就倒推出它必定古老。

sections.heading: 借了，也可以不照它的方向走
paragraphs: 我与癸酉本最大的分歧，在它怎样安放悲剧。它写天下大乱，让许多人物的毁灭发生在战争与劫掠中。我想写的却是：世道不必先变成末日，一个人也会被日常的权势、交易、顾忌和沉默一步步逼到无处可去。
这不是说战争中的悲剧不值得写，而是两种写法追问的事情不同。把一切交给乱世，读者容易把罪责也交给乱世；我想让某些具体的人和具体的关系，仍留在能被看清的地方。
因此，即使借了一个情节的骨架，也未必借它对人物的判断。即使采用了一次相遇，也未必采用同样的结局。哪些取来，哪些反过来写，都需要分开记。
但反过来写，并不能把借鉴注销。新的方向由我负责，原先的提示仍有它的来源。这两件事一起成立，不必争着只留一件。

sections.heading: 如果它完全是今人的作品
paragraphs: 新论文把这个问题放在最不利于项目的条件下问了一遍：假定它不能为任何曹雪芹旧稿作证，眼下的续写有哪些东西得改？
有的情节在前八十回或批语里另有依据，那一层依据仍在。有的细节只是从癸酉本借来，就应当作为对另一部续写的借鉴交代，不能再叫独立旁证。有的字句相同或近似，更需要标明来源或重新写过；不能拿“整体意思已不同”遮过去。
核查的结果也不是“其实没借多少”。相当一部分借来的，正是写作上的东西：情节骨架、细节、场面，还有少数回目、称谓与字句。若为了维护原创的名义，把这些全说成只是偶然相同，读者就更没有理由信任这份说明。
原创不是凭空发生，也不是把所有来处洗净之后才取得资格。它要求的是，新的写法由谁作了选择，借来的部分有没有如实交代，读者能不能看见两者的边界。来源清楚，也不自动免除字句使用上的责任；那仍要逐处处理。

sections.heading: 把账放在故事旁边
paragraphs: 一篇散文不必把全部采择清单摊开。想逐项查的读者，可以去看论文；想先看故事的人，也不必先通过版本争议的考试。但至少应当提前知道，这里有一本被借鉴过的书，以及借鉴所受的限制。
未来公开的后三十回，是我的原创小说，不是曹雪芹佚稿。它会带着我对人物的理解，也带着可以被读者指出的失误。材料研究不能替小说保证成功，小说写得动人也不能替材料说明免账。
因此，这篇暂不以“问题已经解决”作结。清单会随核查继续修订，尚未读到的原件不能写成见过，后来发现的来路也应补入。后续专题还会往下做。
故事放在这里，借鉴的账也放在旁边。读者可以先翻任何一本。

en.title: How Do You Acknowledge Borrowing from a Disputed Book?
en.deck: Naming a debt does not cancel originality. Presenting borrowed material as an independent discovery does deprive the reader of a way to judge.

sections.heading: Another book was on the desk
paragraphs: While writing beyond chapter eighty of Dream of the Red Chamber, I had more than the surviving novel and its early commentary beside me. I also read the text commonly called the Guiyou version, a twenty-eight-chapter continuation with a heavily disputed provenance. I borrowed from it. Readers should know that.

The difficulty is not merely whether to mention its title. After extensive revision, a writer can remember the final decision and forget the initial prompt. A scene acquires different participants; an event changes direction. With time, the result begins to feel as though every part originated at the same desk.
That makes it necessary to look backward. Where did the first suggestion come from? It is now very different may accurately describe the rewriting. It does not answer the question of origin.

sections.heading: Do not let a claimed history do the proving
paragraphs: The Guiyou text circulated online from 2008 and subsequently appeared in differing printed and edited forms. Accounts of its date and authorship disagree. The old manuscript claimed behind it has not been made publicly available for examination, and published scholarship largely treats it as a modern forgery. Those difficulties cannot be omitted because the material is useful.

The project reads it as a later re-creation drawing on an earlier draft. That needs a firm qualification: it is the working hypothesis I adopt, not an established finding about the text’s history. A reader can reject it and still inspect every borrowing.

Not adjudicating authenticity in these essays does not mean authenticity is irrelevant. A modern continuation cannot establish Cao Xueqin’s intentions merely by calling itself an old text. Suitability for a new story and authority as historical evidence are different qualifications.

Keeping them apart makes a more straightforward reading possible. A scene may prompt an idea without becoming evidence of a lost original. A detail may fit the first eighty chapters because a later writer read them well. Fit alone cannot prove antiquity.

sections.heading: Borrowing need not mean following
paragraphs: My largest disagreement with the Guiyou version concerns the setting of its tragedy. It places many characters’ destruction amid political collapse, war, and plunder. I wanted to examine something else: a world need not become an apocalypse for ordinary power, transactions, caution, and silence to leave someone with no way out.

This does not diminish tragedy written about war. It distinguishes the questions two works can ask. Once general chaos explains everything, responsibility can dissolve into that chaos too. I want particular actions and relationships to remain visible.

A borrowed plot outline therefore need not carry the borrowed work’s judgment of a person. An adopted encounter need not reach the same conclusion. What was retained and what was reversed need separate entries.
But reversal does not erase the debt. I am responsible for the new direction; the original prompt still has its source. Both statements can remain true.

sections.heading: Suppose it is entirely modern
paragraphs: The new paper tests the matter under an unfavorable assumption for the project: suppose this text provides no evidence for any draft by Cao Xueqin. What would have to change?

Where an element has independent support in the first eighty chapters or the commentary, that support remains. Where a detail comes only from the Guiyou version, it must be identified as borrowing from another continuation, not independent corroboration. Matching or closely matching wording needs acknowledgment or rewriting. A different overall meaning cannot conceal a verbal debt.

The audit does not conclude that there was hardly any borrowing. Much of what was taken was precisely the material of writing: plot outlines, details, scenes, and a smaller number of chapter titles, labels, and phrases. Calling these accidental similarities in order to defend originality would make the explanation less credible, not more.

Original fiction does not emerge from nowhere. Its claim is not that every source has been washed away, but that someone takes responsibility for the new choices and makes the debts visible. Acknowledging a source also does not automatically resolve questions about the use of its wording. Those still require attention, passage by passage.

sections.heading: Leave the account beside the story
paragraphs: A reader’s essay need not reproduce the complete list of borrowings. Anyone wanting the itemized record can follow the paper; anyone wanting the fiction need not first pass an examination in disputed editions. Both readers should at least know which other book was used and what limits govern that use.

The thirty chapters to be released are my original fiction, not Cao Xueqin’s recovered manuscript. They will carry my interpretation of the people, along with mistakes readers may identify. Source research cannot guarantee that the fiction works. Moving fiction cannot exempt its writer from explaining the sources.

So this essay does not end by declaring the matter closed. The record can change as checking continues. An original document not examined cannot be described as seen, and a debt discovered later must be added. Further studies will follow.
The story belongs on the table. The account of its borrowings belongs beside it. Readers may open either first.
